subject: Alignment: Blue Orchard inference stack, performance targets, and next actions
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@blueorchard.ai>, Ellie Stone <ellie.stone@blueorchard.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Alignment: Blue Orchard inference stack, performance targets, and next actions

Hi Sanjay / Ellie — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. Notes below are based on what we covered; please flag any inaccuracies.

Summary of pain / goals
- Tail latency spikes during business-hours bursts (affects UI refresh for agents).
- Mixed-model footprint: a small / fast general LLM and a larger code-specialized model.
- Need predictable unit cost and per-request SLAs for customer-facing features.

Performance targets discussed
- 95th percentile tail latency target: <= 200 ms for short prompts (< 150 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target: 600 requests / minute for baseline; bursts up to 1800 req/min for ~3–10 minute windows.
- Cold-start tolerance: acceptable up to 2s for deep-models if warm pools are available.

Topology options we walked through
- Dedicated single-region pool (us-west-2) with autoscaling policy capped to maintain SLOs.
- Hybrid: hosted frontend + private/dedicated GPUs for heavy models; prefix/KV cache to reduce repeated token cost.
- Quantized model variants for cost-sensitive routes; fallback to full-precision on quality regressions.

Immediate asks / actions for Blue Orchard
- Confirm the two models you plan to serve (model names + sizes).
- Share a representative sample of request shapes (avg tokens, median, 95th).
- Confirm target region (you indicated us-west-2) and any regulatory constraints (log retention, encryption).

What we (Redwood) will deliver by next touchpoint
- Draft topology diagram (attached: topology-diagram-v2.png) showing warm pool + caching layer.
- Proposal with capacity estimates and cost ranges (attached: blue-orchard-inference-proposal-v1.pdf).
- A proposed perf-test window and list of metrics we will collect (p95/p99, token throughput, kv cache hit rate).

Next steps
1) Sanjay: confirm models + sample request traces (JSON) by EOD Thursday (2027-05-20).
2) We (Aditya/Rishi): prep a perf-run plan targeting May 24–25 and share runbook.
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive (perf + deployment runbook) the week of May 24.

If that reads accurately, I’ll open the HubSpot action and lock the test window.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@blueorchard.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ellie Stone <ellie.stone@blueorchard.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alignment: Blue Orchard inference stack, performance targets, and next actions

Thanks Kimberly — this is great and accurate. A few clarifications from our side:

- Models: we plan to serve llama-3-16 (conversational) and codegen-v1.2-large (code assistance).
- Typical request shape: mean ~120 tokens in, ~60 tokens out. 95th token count ~450.
- Burst profile: we see short bursts of ~30 RPS (peaks) that last 3–7 minutes during market open; sustained baseline is ~10 RPS. Your throughput numbers align with our rough math.
- Region: yes, us-west-2 preferred for data residency and latency to our frontends.
- Compliance: logs should be retained for 90 days; we need encryption-at-rest and role-based access for audit logs.

We will push a sanitized sample trace and a few representative prompt templates to you by EOD Thursday (2027-05-20). For the perf run, can you please include a test plan that exercises both cached prefixes and cold-path requests?

Appreciate the fast follow-up.

— Sanjay
Director, Infrastructure — Blue Orchard AI
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@blueorchard.ai>, Ellie Stone <ellie.stone@blueorchard.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Alignment: Blue Orchard inference stack, performance targets, and next actions

Kim / Rishi — quick internal note that I also forwarded to Blue Orchard:

Plan for perf validation (draft)
- Environment: dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 mirroring their production instance counts (start with 4xA10 equivalent; scale plan included).
- Load profile: replay sanitized traces + synthetic bursts to reach 30 RPS peaks (3–7 min) and sustained 10 RPS baseline.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency (token and request), token throughput (tokens/sec), KV cache hit rate, model quantization quality delta (sample prompts).
- Warm-pool strategy: maintain a small warm pool for the large model; measure cold-start penalty across varying warm pool sizes (0, 2, 6 instances).
- Autoscaling config suggestion: aggressive scale-up threshold at 60% GPU util with preemptive warm pool scaling for burst windows.

Action items for us (owners)
- Aditya: build runbook, perf scripts, and steady-state cost estimate (due 2027-05-21).
- Rishi: prepare quantized vs fp32 quality comparison plan and guardrails (due 2027-05-21).
- Kim: confirm test window with Blue Orchard (you have the ask).

Two quick questions for the customer to include in test artifacts:
1) A set of 5 high-priority prompt templates we should treat as non-negotiable quality gates.
2) Confirmation on acceptable p99 latency upper bound during bursts (is 500ms acceptable for codegen?).

I’ll have the initial runbook ready for review by Friday morning.

— Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay.mehta@blueorchard.ai>, Ellie Stone <ellie.stone@blueorchard.ai>

Subject: Re: Alignment: Blue Orchard inference stack, performance targets, and next actions

Appreciate the confirmations, Sanjay. Finalizing mutual action plan and deadlines below — please reply with any blockers.

Mutual action plan (finalized)
- Blue Orchard (Sanjay / Ellie): provide sanitized request traces, 5 priority prompt templates, and confirm p99 acceptable upper bound for codegen by 2027-05-20 EOD. (Owner: Sanjay)
- Redwood (Aditya / Rishi): deliver runbook, perf scripts, cost envelope, and quantization comparison by 2027-05-21. (Owners: Aditya / Rishi)
- Perf window: 2027-05-24 to 2027-05-25. Redwood will run tests and share results within 48 hours of completion.
- Follow-up technical review: 60-minute meeting to review perf results and finalize topology on 2027-05-27 (proposed slots sent via calendar). (Owner: Kimberly)

Attachments: blue-orchard-inference-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal + sizing), topology-diagram-v2.png (draft topology). I’ll push the HubSpot action with deal BO-2027-041 and include the above milestones.

If all good, I’ll lock the perf window and send calendar invites.

Best — Kim
